newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bomb blasts Colombian banana growers' offices.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blasts Colombian banana growers' offices.

text.p: A car-bomb exploded in an upscale district of the northwestern Colombian city of Medellin on Tuesday, injuring at least six people, police said.

The attack was directed at offices of the banana producers' association AUGURA, which has it base in the violence-torn region of Uraba where leftist guerrillas and right-wing paramilitary groups have killed with impunity for years.

The Radionet radio network said Col. Jose Toro, operational head of the Medellin police, told local media the bomb had been concealed in a car parked outside the AUGURA offices. But other media said the explosive may have been thrown from a passing motorcycle.

A Bogota-based spokeswoman for AUGURA told Reuters: "I have just been in contact with our representatives in Medellin. There was an attack but we don't know any more details as yet. It appears there are injuries."
Leftist rebels in Uraba, a banana-growing region, have frequently accused banana growers and the main banana workers' union Sintrainagro of backing right-wing paramilitary groups.
